compareCandidate.label: Arteries vs. veins
compareCandidate.description: Arteries carry blood away from the heart under high pressure (thick walls). Veins carry blood back toward the heart with one-way valves (thinner walls). Capillaries are where the exchange happens.

processes: Carrying blood away from the heart (arteries)
Carrying blood back to the heart (veins)
plainLanguageExplanation: Blood vessels are the tubes that carry blood around the body. There are three main types. Arteries carry blood away from the heart; they have thick, stretchy walls because the heart's pumping makes blood flow through them at high pressure. Veins carry blood back toward the heart; they have thinner walls and small one-way valves to stop blood flowing backward. Capillaries are the tiniest vessels, so thin that materials can pass through their walls - this is where oxygen, nutrients, and waste are exchanged with the cells. So the network works like this: arteries are the highways out, capillaries are the driveways where the delivery happens, and veins are the highways back.

whyItMatters: Blood vessels deliver oxygen and food to every cell and carry waste away. Understanding arteries, veins, and capillaries explains your pulse, why veins look blue through the skin, and how every part of you stays supplied.
didYouKnow: If all your blood vessels were laid end to end, they would stretch about 96,000 kilometers - more than twice around the Earth.
